title: Airbnb illustration guidelines, “Your Face Here” (Jennifer Hom)
lede: Airbnb’s head of illustration explains its 2018 illustration redesign, which kept flat, lightweight figures but rejected the rainbow-colored skin of the tech style.
summary: A Big Tech illustration system of the same years that chose realistic skin tones and body types over rainbow figures. Documented, 2018.

source.label: Airbnb Design (Medium): Jennifer Hom, “Your Face Here”, 18 December 2018

evidence.note: Read the article text through a Wayback Machine copy; medium.com returned HTTP 403 to scripts. The article images did not load in that copy, so no illustration was inspected.

styles.note: Partial fit, and a counterpoint: a flat, minimal Big Tech illustration system from the style’s peak years, whose author explicitly rejected the “rainbow-colored figures” that define the style.

context: Hom joined Airbnb in October 2017 to redesign its illustration style. She lists four principles: “grounded, scalable, lightweight, and diverse”, and says the style is “fairly minimal and lightweight” with “intentional white space”. [Airbnb Design](https://medium.com/airbnb-design/your-face-here-9aa1d4970d6c).

She describes a common solution in tech illustration as “a metaphor for diversity through rainbow-colored figures … colored in red, blue, yellow, orange, purple, and green. Put simply, they’re not real.” She tried this in early drafts and rejected it. [Airbnb Design](https://medium.com/airbnb-design/your-face-here-9aa1d4970d6c).

She also rejects “cartoon people outlined in blue or grey”, and asks for reference photos for every person drawn and for different races, ages, abilities, and body types. [Airbnb Design](https://medium.com/airbnb-design/your-face-here-9aa1d4970d6c).
interpretation: The article is a contemporary insider’s description of the style’s central device, non-natural skin, as a way to avoid questions of race. It helps separate the style from other flat tech illustration of the same years.
borrow: When figures must represent real users, use a real range of skin tones and body types; keep the flat fills and white space.
